dynarules 0.1.0 — demo

Which actions co-occur, and which follow one another?

A synthetic event log: 60 students, each producing a coded session. Half follow a plan-first strategy (plan precedes discuss precedes reflect, with noise); half act haphazardly.

make_session <- function(strategic) {
  noise <- sample(c("search", "read", "note"), 3, replace = TRUE)
  core <- if (strategic) c("plan", "discuss", "reflect")
          else sample(c("plan", "discuss", "reflect"))
  idx <- sort(sample(6, 3))
  out <- character(6)
  out[idx] <- core
  out[-idx] <- noise
  out
}
log <- data.frame(
  student = rep(sprintf("s%02d", 1:60), each = 6),
  code = unlist(lapply(1:60, function(i) make_session(i <= 30))),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
head(log, 8)
##   student    code
## 1     s01  search
## 2     s01  search
## 3     s01    plan
## 4     s01  search
## 5     s01 discuss
## 6     s01 reflect
## 7     s02    note
## 8     s02    plan

Transactions: the unit of analysis is explicit

tr <- transactions(log, actor = "student", action = "code")
tr
## <dyna_transactions>  60 transactions | 6 items | unit: session
##   mean events per transaction: 6.0 (ordered sequences kept)
summary(tr)
##      item count   support
## 1 discuss    60 1.0000000
## 2    note    42 0.7000000
## 3    plan    60 1.0000000
## 4    read    39 0.6500000
## 5 reflect    60 1.0000000
## 6  search    46 0.7666667

Co-occurrence rules

fit_co <- dynarules(tr, type = "cooccurrence",
                    min_support = 0.2, min_confidence = 0.5, min_lift = 0)
fit_co
## <dynarules> cooccurrence rules  [414 rules | 6 items | 60 transactions]
##   support >= 0.20 | confidence >= 0.50 | lift >= 0.00 | max length 5
## 
##   Top rules (by lift):
##      1. {note} => {discuss}  (sup=0.700 conf=1.000 lift=1.00)
##      2. {discuss} => {plan}  (sup=1.000 conf=1.000 lift=1.00)
##      3. {plan} => {discuss}  (sup=1.000 conf=1.000 lift=1.00)
##      4. {note} => {plan}  (sup=0.700 conf=1.000 lift=1.00)
##      5. {read} => {discuss}  (sup=0.650 conf=1.000 lift=1.00)
##      6. {read} => {plan}  (sup=0.650 conf=1.000 lift=1.00)
##      7. {discuss} => {reflect}  (sup=1.000 conf=1.000 lift=1.00)
##      8. {reflect} => {discuss}  (sup=1.000 conf=1.000 lift=1.00)
##      9. {note} => {reflect}  (sup=0.700 conf=1.000 lift=1.00)
##     10. {plan} => {reflect}  (sup=1.000 conf=1.000 lift=1.00)
##     ... and 404 more rules (see rules(x))
plot(fit_co)

Sequential rules: order as evidence

fit_seq <- dynarules(tr, type = "sequential",
                     min_support = 0.3, min_confidence = 0.3,
                     min_lift = 0, max_length = 3)
fit_seq
## <dynarules> sequential rules  [28 rules | 6 items | 60 transactions]
##   support >= 0.30 | confidence >= 0.30 | lift >= 0.00 | max length 3
## 
##   Top rules (by lift):
##      1. {plan -> discuss} => {reflect}  (sup=0.550 conf=0.825 lift=0.83)
##      2. {discuss} => {reflect -> search}  (sup=0.300 conf=0.300 lift=0.78)
##      3. {read} => {reflect}  (sup=0.500 conf=0.769 lift=0.77)
##      4. {discuss} => {reflect}  (sup=0.767 conf=0.767 lift=0.77)
##      5. {plan} => {search}  (sup=0.583 conf=0.583 lift=0.76)
##      6. {plan} => {reflect}  (sup=0.750 conf=0.750 lift=0.75)
##      7. {plan} => {discuss -> reflect}  (sup=0.550 conf=0.550 lift=0.72)
##      8. {search} => {reflect}  (sup=0.533 conf=0.696 lift=0.70)
##      9. {plan} => {search -> reflect}  (sup=0.367 conf=0.367 lift=0.69)
##     10. {plan} => {discuss}  (sup=0.667 conf=0.667 lift=0.67)
##     ... and 18 more rules (see rules(x))
rules(fit_seq, min_lift = 1, top = 8)
## [1] antecedent     consequent     support        confidence     lift          
## [6] conviction     count          n_transactions
## <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)
plot(fit_seq)

Is the order real? Permutation test (order-shuffling null)

The null preserves exactly which actions co-occur and destroys only their order, so surviving rules are informative beyond co-occurrence.

pt <- permute_rules(fit_seq, iter = 200, seed = 1)
pt
## <dynarules_perm> 200 permutations | null: within-transaction order shuffle | BH correction
##   9 of 28 rules significant at adjusted p < .05
## 
##   Rules (by adjusted p):
##      1. {plan -> discuss} => {reflect}  lift=0.83 (null 0.32)  p_adj=0.0232 *
##      2. {discuss} => {reflect -> search}  lift=0.78 (null 0.35)  p_adj=0.0232 *
##      3. {discuss} => {reflect}  lift=0.77 (null 0.50)  p_adj=0.0232 *
##      4. {plan} => {reflect}  lift=0.75 (null 0.50)  p_adj=0.0232 *
##      5. {plan} => {discuss -> reflect}  lift=0.72 (null 0.33)  p_adj=0.0232 *
##      6. {plan} => {search -> reflect}  lift=0.69 (null 0.35)  p_adj=0.0232 *
##      7. {plan} => {search}  lift=0.76 (null 0.58)  p_adj=0.0310 *
##      8. {plan} => {discuss}  lift=0.67 (null 0.50)  p_adj=0.0310 *
##      9. {plan -> search} => {reflect}  lift=0.63 (null 0.35)  p_adj=0.0310 *
##     10. {read} => {reflect}  lift=0.77 (null 0.57)  p_adj=0.0836
##     ... and 18 more rules
plot(pt)

Are the rules stable? Bootstrap

bs <- bootstrap_rules(fit_seq, iter = 100, seed = 1)
bs
## <dynarules_boot> 100 resamples | 28 rules | 95% CIs

Rules as a network

net <- as_network(fit_seq, weight = "lift")
net
## <dynarules_net> rules_sequential network
##   nodes: 6   edges: 21   (directed; weight = lift, max)
round(net$weights, 2)
